nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Strong subtropical sun drives plant growth on the open Chaco plain, but it also dries the land through the long dry season.

nodes.name: Seasonal rain
nodes.desc: Rain falls mostly in one wet season followed by a long dry spell, so plant growth and water for animals come in pulses.

nodes.name: Timane River and waterholes
nodes.desc: The Timane River runs through old channels toward Cerro Leon and feeds an inland basin; seasonal pools matter for wildlife in a dry land.

nodes.name: Soil and nutrients
nodes.desc: Sandy and clay soils of the plain hold the nutrients that trees and grasses draw on, topped up as dead matter breaks down.

nodes.name: Fungi, bacteria and termites
nodes.desc: Break down fallen wood, leaf litter and carcasses, returning nutrients to the soil.

nodes.name: White carob (algarrobo)
nodes.desc: A thorny, drought-tolerant Chaco tree that bears sugary pods; mammals and birds eat the pods and fruit.

nodes.name: Toothpick cactus
nodes.desc: A tall columnar cactus of the dry Chaco, one of the succulents that store water through the dry season.

nodes.name: Signalgrass
nodes.desc: Grasses of open patches among the thorn forest, one of the well-recorded plant groups near the park; seeds feed doves and others.

nodes.name: Chacoan peccary
nodes.desc: A large wild pig of the dry Chaco that feeds heavily on cacti and other tough plants. Once thought extinct, it is now known from the Chaco.

nodes.name: Lowland tapir
nodes.desc: A large browsing mammal that eats leaves and fruit and spreads seeds through its dung.

nodes.name: Gray brocket
nodes.desc: A small forest deer that browses leaves and fruit; reported as a viable population in the park.

nodes.name: Eared dove
nodes.desc: A seed-eating dove found in open country, and a common prey bird for small raptors.

nodes.name: Turquoise-fronted parrot
nodes.desc: A parrot of Chaco woodland that eats seeds and fruit.

nodes.name: Southern three-banded armadillo
nodes.desc: An armadillo that can roll into a ball; it feeds mainly on ants and termites and some plant matter.

nodes.name: Leafcutter ants
nodes.desc: Colonies cut leaves to grow fungus underground, moving plant matter into the soil.

nodes.name: Crab-eating fox
nodes.desc: An opportunistic canid that eats fruit, insects and small vertebrates.

nodes.name: Black-legged seriema
nodes.desc: A long-legged ground bird of the Chaco that hunts insects, snakes and other small animals.

nodes.name: Baron's green racer
nodes.desc: A slender, rear-fanged snake of Chaco woodland that preys on lizards, birds and small mammals.

nodes.name: Savanna hawk
nodes.desc: A hawk of open country that hunts reptiles, small mammals and other prey from perches.

nodes.name: Black vulture
nodes.desc: A common scavenger that cleans up carcasses across open country and woodland.

nodes.name: Jaguar
nodes.desc: The largest cat of the Americas. The park may hold one of the southernmost viable jaguar populations; it hunts peccaries, tapirs and deer.

nodes.name: Puma
nodes.desc: A widespread cat reported with a viable population in the park; it preys on deer, peccaries and armadillos.
